item.title: Their Mars window is a TV — clip from Encore: A Year In Mars Dune Alpha
item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】火星栖息舱的窗户其实是一台电视：播着舱外火星日出的视频，太阳升起、舱影、夜里星星，最后落到一句话——几乎就是火星。 【Reels 角度】他们的火星窗户是一台电视：先给画面，再给几乎是火星这句结尾。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. item.content:encoded: We have a window that we use, air quotes around the word window, that it uses a TV with a video feed of the outside of our habitat. And we can see the Martian sunrise with it out the window, and then the sun basically goes over our head and we eventually see the shadow of our habitat on the ground and eventually, throughout night we see the stars. And it's really pretty. If I could sum up Chapea in just a couple of words, the words would be, almost Mars.

item.title: A penny in a clear pool: how we see dark matter — clip from Encore: Welcome to the Dark Side (800.0-851.5s)
item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】看不见的暗物质怎么被看见：想象晴天里一池清水，池底的硬币看起来变了形——光被水弯折了；远方星系的光被暗物质弯折，也是同一个道理。 【Reels 角度】看不见的东西怎么证明它存在？一枚池底的硬币告诉你：光被弯折的地方，就有暗物质。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. Reusable with no NASA endorsement implied; full-episode music cues do not appear in this speech segment. 【来源】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-dark-side-encore/ 【采集日（北京时间）】2026-10-27 【发布时间精度】exact_encore（Inherits parent original publish date (Megaphone RSS Tue, 22 Sep 2026 13:03:00 -0000; episode originally published 2023); clip itself was modelled 2026-10-27 Beijing, GUID does not use collection time.） 【父集 GUID】urn:podcast:nasa.gov:curious-universe:roman-dark-side-encore 【父集链接】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-dark-side-encore/ 【片段】原集 800.0-851.5 秒，51.5 秒，原声，未加 BGM，文件：clips/nasa-roman-dark-side-clip-penny.mp3
item.content:encoded: And I can use an analogy here. Imagine you're standing on a very calm day in front of a very crystal clear pool, and you throw a penny to the bottom of the pool. Now, you can't really see the water because it's crystal clear, but you can see the penny at the bottom of the pool and anyone who's done this knows that you see a distorted view of that penny. It doesn't appear as it would just on the ground. And that's because the light from the penny is traveling through the water and the light is bent by the water. So in this analogy, that penny is like the distant galaxy and the water is like the dark matter. So we don't actually see the dark matter. You don't actually see the water, but you know it's there. You know the water is there because you see a distorted view of the penny. And we know the dark matter is there because we see a distorted image of these background galaxies.

item.title: Ferdinand Hassler: the first superintendent of the Coast Survey — clip from Origins of NOAA's National Ocean Service (236.9-289.5s)
item.description: 【节目】NOAA Ocean Podcast 【主题】ocean-environment 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】首任局长 Hassler：学法律出身的瑞士移民，因测绘经验被杰斐逊看中，成了海岸测量局第一任局长。 【Reels 角度】学法律的人怎么成了美国第一个海洋测量局长？瑞士移民 Hassler 的故事。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NOAA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. Reusable with no NOAA endorsement implied. 【来源】https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/sep26/nop86-nos-origins.html 【采集日（北京时间）】2026-10-26 【发布时间精度】date_only（Inherits parent original publish date (NOAA page DC.date.created 2026-9-21, date only); clip itself was modelled 2026-10-26 Beijing, GUID does not use collection time.） 【父集 GUID】urn:podcast:oceanservice.noaa.gov:podcast:sep26:nop86-nos-origins 【父集链接】https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/sep26/nop86-nos-origins.html 【片段】原集 236.9-289.5 秒，52.6 秒，原声，未加 BGM，文件：clips/noaa-nos-origins-86-clip-hassler.mp3
item.content:encoded: That's right. So the first superintendent of the Coast Survey was a Swiss émigre named Ferdinand Hassler. And Hassler had studied law but then decided science was his passion. So he studied math. He had done a survey of one of the Cantons in Switzerland and had great experience. But he decided that he wanted to emigrate to the United States, and he felt that he had real skills to contribute to the development of the nation. And he was suggested to Thomas Jefferson. Jefferson, like many of the founding fathers, had a real scientific bent and saw a talented, experienced person who he could trust to establish this agency. He saw that in Hassler and appointed him.

item.title: We just witnessed the most unbelievable, picture-perfect launch — clip from Roman Series: Liftoff! (920.0-958.6s)
item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】等了二十多年，Roman 终于升空：科学家 Dominic 说，这次发射美得难以想象——曾经只存在于图纸上的机器，真的飞进了太空，现在它属于所有人。 【Reels 角度】为一台望远镜等了二十多年，发射成功那一刻他只说了一句话：这简直不敢相信。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. Reusable with no NASA endorsement implied; full-episode music cues do not appear in this speech segment. 【来源】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-launch-podcast/ 【采集日（北京时间）】2026-10-27 【发布时间精度】exact（Inherits parent original publish date (Megaphone RSS Sat, 05 Sep 2026 12:36:00 -0000); clip itself was modelled 2026-10-27 Beijing, GUID does not use collection time.） 【父集 GUID】urn:podcast:nasa.gov:curious-universe:roman-liftoff 【父集链接】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-launch-podcast/ 【片段】原集 920.0-958.6 秒，38.6 秒，原声，未加 BGM，文件：clips/nasa-roman-liftoff-clip-picture-perfect.mp3
item.content:encoded: We just witnessed the most unbelievable, picture-perfect launch that I could ever imagine. And in a way, even though it's been so many years, I never quite wrapped my head around the idea that someday this would happen. And watching Roman ascend into the sky was unlike anything I could explain or describe. Because I could never convince myself that it was actually real. That we would manifest this amazing machine and get it into space. But we did. And now it's there for everybody.

item.title: Monitor as a testbed: new 3D imaging can spread to other wrecks — clip from USS Monitor 3D Mapping (559.7-604.5s)
item.description: 【节目】NOAA Ocean Podcast 【主题】ocean-environment 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】Monitor 当试验场：这套新成像技术不只拍 Monitor，还能用到更多沉船、沉没飞机甚至原住民遗址——关键是又快又准。 【Reels 角度】沉船变试验场：1862 年的 Monitor 试成功的新成像，能复制到别的沉船上吗？答案是能，而且很快。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NOAA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. Reusable with no NOAA endorsement implied. 【来源】https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/aug26/nop85-uss-monitor-3d-mapping.html 【采集日（北京时间）】2026-10-26 【发布时间精度】date_only（Inherits parent original publish date (NOAA page DC.date.created 2026-8-21, date only); clip itself was modelled 2026-10-26 Beijing, GUID does not use collection time.） 【父集 GUID】urn:podcast:oceanservice.noaa.gov:podcast:aug26:nop85-uss-monitor-3d-mapping 【父集链接】https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/aug26/nop85-uss-monitor-3d-mapping.html 【片段】原集 559.7-604.5 秒，44.8 秒，原声，未加 BGM，文件：clips/noaa-uss-monitor-3d-85-clip-testbed.mp3
item.content:encoded: Do you suppose this new imaging technology will be used on more shipwrecks? Like saltwater and freshwater? Yeah, I hope by basically using Monitor as a testbed, and that's one of the wonderful things about Monitor, that where it's always been pushing technology innovation from 1862 to today, bringing all those new technologies to bear. That, you know, people would look at the example of what we achieved on Monitor with Northrop Grumman using this technology and how it can now be used and applied to other sites as well. You know, whether that be shipwrecks, maybe it's sunken aircraft. You know, maybe there's sunken indigenous sites. You know, just the technology and the resolution we can see for these things is mind-blowing. And the fact that we can collect that so quickly with the AUV, too, is very special.

item.title: Break the Grip of the Rip: swim parallel, not back — clip from Rip Currents (335.1-380.9s)
item.description: 【节目】NOAA Ocean Podcast 【主题】ocean-environment 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】离岸流自救口令：别直游回岸、别跟水流硬拼，沿岸平行游出再斜着回岸；这套指引已让约 90% 受访海滩游客知晓，但每年仍约有 100 人因此溺亡。 【Reels 角度】被离岸流卷走先别慌：平行游出才是活路，配 90% 与每年约 100 起的数据钩子。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NOAA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. Reusable with no NOAA endorsement implied. 【来源】https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/june23/nop66-rip-currents.html 【采集日（北京时间）】2026-10-24 【发布时间精度】date_only（Inherits parent original publish date (NOAA list 28 Jun 2023, date only); clip itself was modelled 2026-10-24 Beijing, GUID does not use collection time.） 【父集 GUID】urn:podcast:oceanservice.noaa.gov:podcast:june23:nop66-rip-currents 【父集链接】https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/june23/nop66-rip-currents.html 【片段】原集 335.1-380.9 秒，45.8 秒，原声，未加 BGM，文件：clips/noaa-rip-currents-clip-335-381.mp3
item.content:encoded: break the grip of the rip, you see an image of a rip current, and it gives guidance to people on what to do if you're caught in a rip current, which is to stay calm, don't swim straight back to shore, don't fight the current, swim out of the current along the beach, you're out of the current and then back to the beach at an angle. And that guidance has largely been pretty successful. We did some surveys recently and found something like 90% of those surveyed, of those beach goers that we surveyed, were generally aware of rip currents and what to do if they're caught in one. But despite that success, as I mentioned, we're still seeing the same number of rip current drownings every year, something like 100 rip current drownings per year.
